title: Membership in a color class
statement: Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $\\pi:\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}\\to\\{0,\\ldots,m-1\\}$ be a map, and let $j$ and $i$ belong to the respective sets of indices. Then $i$ belongs to the color class of $j$ if and only if $\\pi(i)=j$.
hypotheses_covered: $\\pi$ maps the $n$ coordinate indices to the $m$ color indices
replaced: Let $n,m\ge0$, $\pi\colon[n]\to[m]$, $j\in[m]$, and $i\in[n]$. For $F_j(\pi)=\{u\in[n]:\pi(u)=j\}$, one has $i\in F_j(\pi)$ if and only if $\pi(i)=j$.
